_comment: Twenty large companies, one per industry, chosen so that no two share a
network-estate shape: a grocery chain, a parcel network, a bank branch
estate, a plant-and-lab estate and a mine site are different problems,
and an estimator that only ever sees stores is not being tested.
industry is the code the case is researched under. Every one of these
which are keyed by it - an industry the seed does not know falls back to
DEFAULT, and the estate stops differentiating. Entity resolution proposes
its own industry on the candidate; this is the fallback and the check.
in_scope_countries is deliberately a handful per company rather than the
whole group footprint. The countries are where the estate is dense AND
where reference.unit_cost_prior has approved rates, because a country
with sites and no rate card prices nothing and only lowers coverage.
declared_footprint is a public-disclosure fallback, used only if research
returns no promotable site counts. The manifest records which was used.

excluded.reason: the finding counts a satellite IT room in Dublin, named in an IT contractor's project page alongside Slough and Dundee. A room of equipment inside a building Tesco already occupies is not a site, and pricing it as a DC both invents a building and gives it a data centre's bandwidth.
the only source is a warehouse fit-out company's listicle of large buildings, which names one Dublin facility and states no count. The finding's own note says the total Irish DC count was not found.

a drop-off counter inside a third-party retailer. The premises are the host's and so is the access line; a DHL scanner on cellular is a device cost, not a site circuit. Same basis as the UPS Store network.
Fintro is a franchise network - independently operated agents, so the connectivity is not BNP's cost. The retained Belgian branches are declared separately.
the 1,474 retail branches in the registration document are the same network this spec declares as 1,600 FR BRANCH sites.

the 2,500 agencies are the Nordost sales region alone - the sources say 'in den neuen Bundeslaendern' and 'im Vertriebsgebiet Nordost' - promoted as a German national count, and the figure is a pre-closure baseline against which 430 agencies were due to shut in 2025. Whether a tied agent's connectivity is Allianz's cost is the separate question referred on the French agencies.
31 branches of Allianz Bank Financial Advisors from a single aggregator, with no evidence settling whether the 400 declared Italian branches already include them.

an agent general is self-employed, leases their own premises and buys their own access line; Allianz reaches them over it. The STORE archetype buys a broadband circuit with 5G backup and Allianz does not buy 2,516 of those. Same basis as the UPS Store network and BNP's Fintro branches, both already excluded.

excluded.reason: the finding is labelled 'CN total plants (vehicle + component, incl. all JVs)' and the breakdown names 6 SAIC-Volkswagen and 6 FAW-Volkswagen vehicle plants. Both are 50/50 joint ventures - separate companies, equity-accounted rather than consolidated - and this case's perimeter is GROUP_CONSOLIDATED. A JV buys its own connectivity, which is the basis that excluded UPS franchises, Fintro branches, Allianz tied agents and Shell's dealer forecourts.

excluded.reason: the 1,916 branded retail fuel sites are the same forecourts this spec declares as 1,900 DE SERVICE_POINT sites. Separately, branded is not operated - the question referred on the Dutch forecourts - but the double count stands whichever way that is ruled.

the 662 branded forecourts are the same sites this spec declares as 500 NL SERVICE_POINT. Referred first on whether a dealer-owned forecourt is Shell's cost, which is still an open question; the double count is a second and sufficient reason to keep the row out whichever way that is ruled.

not because the wind farms are not Iberdrola's - they are, and they do carry a connection it pays for - but because pricing 40 of them at the PLANT profile asserts a factory of 60 users on a 100 Mbps dual-access circuit where there is an unmanned SCADA link. That is operational-technology connectivity, a different cost pool from the enterprise access layer this model prices, and consistent with the substations, nodes and towers already refused. If OT connectivity enters scope they return under their own archetype, not PLANT.

the five comes from an apprenticeship announcement - 287 apprentices across five German facilities - which counts sites taking apprentices rather than sites. The group reports 34 facilities worldwide with no German split.

excluded.reason: research now returns 200 for this pair, on a unit reading 'production plants at Ludwigshafen site' - the ~200 production plants on BASF's single Ludwigshafen Verbund site, promoted as 200 German premises. Identical in kind to the Antwerp row excluded at 50, and NOT caught by the within/inside unit guard, because this one says 'at' a named site rather than 'within' one. That is why this exclusion is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces. The earlier reason described a researched 54 labelled 'all site types, Germany'; that finding is no longer what this pair returns, and the text is replaced rather than left citing a figure that no longer exists.

the finding's own unit reads 'production facilities within Antwerp site' and its source says about 50 Produktionsbetriebe on one 6 square kilometre site. Fifty production units inside a single Verbund site are not fifty Belgian premises, and pricing them at the PLANT profile asserts fifty access circuits BASF does not buy. Same basis as Tesco's satellite IT room and the substations this workflow already refuses.

the finding is 'Private 5G campus network - Schwarzheide site (OT layer)'. A 5G campus network is a private on-premises mobile network, not a campus: the word is a telecom term and the CAMPUS archetype means a research or manufacturing campus carrying thousands of people. Schwarzheide is an existing BASF German site already inside the declared estate, so this adds a network deployment as though it were a premises.

excluded.reason: the only German DC finding is dated 2002 and labelled 'IBM-era regional DC'. Its Swiss sibling at Bussigny carries the same 2002 date and the words 'sold to Orllati', and a third finding records no Nestle-owned DC in France at all - so the DC evidence for this company describes an outsourcing estate that has been disposed of.

the 2,624 dialysis clinics the 20-F reports are the same network this spec declares as 2,600 US BRANCH sites. The merge keys on (country, archetype), so a second archetype adds them rather than reconciling them, and the US estate would carry both.

excluded.reason: the researched 95 is a 2016 factory count labelled 'lower bound', predating the Siemens Energy spin-off in 2020 and the Healthineers listing. Ten years stale and pre-divestiture.
the German distribution branches were DIVESTED to STARK Group in 2019 and are no longer Saint-Gobain sites. Research labels them so and the label is not carried past promotion.
the UK distribution branches were DIVESTED to STARK Group in 2023. The French builders' merchants are retained and stay declared.

SGDB France's points de vente are the same builders' merchant network this spec declares as 900 FR WAREHOUSE sites - a trade counter and a yard at one address. The German and British merchants show the same pairing and were excluded as divested; the French ones are retained, so the collision is visible here instead.

excluded.reason: research types a bank's branches as STORE - it returned a 222 national total and a state-by-state breakdown of the same network. They are already declared as BRANCH, so promoting them adds the same branches a second time.

UNFI's 10-K states the ~60,000 customer locations it SUPPLIES - independent retailers buying from it, not sites it operates. Its own retail banners (Cub Foods, Shoppers) are declared explicitly instead.
the researched 4 is a count of DC CLOSURES and consolidations in FY2026 - Allentown PA, a west-region DC, Racine/Sturtevant WI. Sites being shut, added as sites.
the UPS Store network is franchised - independently owned and operated, so its connectivity is not UPS's cost. Research finds ~5,600 of them in the US alone.

excluded.reason: 587 Toyota dealerships in India. A dealership is an independently owned business selling under the brand - it leases its own premises and buys its own access line - which is the basis that excluded 5,603 UPS Store franchises, 182 BNP Fintro branches and 2,516 Allianz tied agents.

the 520 Indian branches are the same network this spec declares as IN BRANCH, typed STORE by research. The merge keys on (country, archetype), so a second archetype adds the branches again rather than correcting the count - the Fresenius, Saint-Gobain, Shell and BNP collision over again. The declared figure is corrected to 520 instead.
